la:verb:obaudio.gloss: to obey, yield obedience to (+dative of person obeyed)
la:verb:obaudio.html:
ŏb-audĭo, ii, 4, v. a., for oboedio,
to obey (post-class.); constr. with dat. or absol.
With dat.: alicui,.—
Absol.: Adam non obaudiit,.—With acc.: obaudite me,.—Hence, ŏbaudĭens, entis, P. a., obedient (eccl. Lat. for oboediens).— Comp.: quid obaudientius esse potest, quam ut, etc.,.

la:verb:obambulo.gloss: to walk up to or close to
senses: to walk up to or close to
la:verb:obambulo.html:
ŏb-ambŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
, to walk before or near any thing, to go past (not in Cic. or Cæs.); constr. with dat. or acc.: obambulare adversum alios ambulare, et quasi ambulanti sese opponere, Paul. ex Müll.
With dat.: obambulare muris,: gymnasio,: nec (lupus) gregibus nocturnus obambulat, walk or prowl about, .—
With acc.: urbem,: totam fremebundus obambulat Aetnam,: gymnasia, (al. gymnasio).—
Transf., in gen., to go or walk about, wander: neu noctu irem obambulatum,: ante vallum,: sermone imperfecto,: in herbis,: praeter os,.—Absol.: cum solus obambulet,; .
la:verb:obambulo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:noun:obaeratus.gloss: involved in debt, in bondage on account of debt
senses: involved in debt, in bondage on account of debt
a person involved in debt, a debtor
la:noun:obaeratus.html:
ŏb-aerātus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
involved in debt, in bondage on account of debt (class.): liber, qui suas operas in servitute pro pecuniā quādam debebat, dum solveret, nexus vocatur, ut ab aere obaeratus, Müll.: tenuis et obaeratus,.—Comp.: quanto quis obaeratior, aegrius distrahebant,the more deeply in debt,.—
Subst.: ŏbaerā-tus, i, m., a person involved in debt, a debtor: obaeratos liberare, * : Orgetorix omnes clientes obaeratosque suos eodem conduxit,; .
